body:
maya: Noticed an org-level quota bump during the routing-policy canary this morning. ~3.8% of traffic moved to org fallback for a 12m window. Saw this at ~07:14 UTC. log snippet: `auth: attribution=fallback scope=org reason=missing_x-project-id token_short=af3c2`

trent: Oof. Which header are we expecting? I thought the proxy was supposed to translate `x-project-id` into the internal claim.

li: We changed sanitization to drop unknown `x-*` headers in the last proxy patch (for security). That likely stripped `x-project-id`. I added a note in the PR but must've missed the follow-up.

maya: Confirmed upstream sends `x-project-id: proj-900` and after proxy we see nothing. We still have the auth JWT with a project claim, but mapping code currently prefers header over token claim — so header drop triggers fallback to org.

ops-bot: alert: org:org-12 quota-soft-threshold crossed at 07:22 UTC. Paging oncall.

clare: Immediate mitigation: 1) disable header-preference in mapping service 2) revert proxy sanitization in canary regions 3) throttle canary until we validate. Any objections?

trent: +1 to disable preference. Also suggest adding a unit test asserting header passthrough: `assert proxy.forwarded_headers includes "x-project-id"` in integration harness.

li: I'll open PRs. PR#4982 will revert the sanitization change in canary, PR#4983 will flip mapping precedence to token claim first if header missing, and PR#4984 will add the test.

maya: For telemetry, can we emit `redwood.authz.attribution` with label=source:(header|token|fallback) and have a graph of header_vs_token_ratio over time? Need to detect regressions automatically.

clare: yes. Also add a sampled event (0.5%) with `token_fingerprint` + `route` + `fallback_reason` to S3 for postmortem. Ensure we strip any user ids.

kevin-support: If customers were billed differently due to org attribution, we need a quick export of affected traces to support. Can you include `request_id` and time range?

maya: I'll run a query over the 12m window and produce a CSV of request_id, route, prior_attribution. Sharing with you by EOD.

trent: Suggest a canary guard: stop rollout if org attribution increases by >1.5% absolute or >150% relative over baseline for 5m. Keep it conservative.

li: Implementing guard in rollout service; will add prometheus alert and automated rollback hook.

clare: Console UX: add a small inline help copy next to the routing toggle: "Routing preference may affect billing attribution; enable only in canary and monitor project attribution panel." Also add a tenant-facing note in release notes.

maya: Good. Also let's be explicit in our docs about precedence: header > token > fallback is fine, but header must be preserved by any proxy step. If we keep header preference, proxies must whitelist `x-project-id`.

trent: Action items recap: li -> PRs 4982/4983/4984 + rollout guard; clare -> telemetry schema + sampled event pipeline; maya -> logs CSV + support handoff; trent -> add integration test to canary harness.

li: Revert PR landed in canary at 08:00 UTC, alerts quieted. Will work on the rest this afternoon.

maya: Thanks. We'll reconvene after metrics show stable attribution for 24h before resuming broad rollout. :white_check_mark:
